summary.title: Sample Web App
summary.description: Draft threat model generated by ThreatForge.

threats.title: Process accepts requests without verifying caller identity
threats.description: Sample Web App Service handles requests but does not authenticate its caller, allowing a spoofed client to act as a trusted one.
threats.mitigation: Authenticate every request to this process; reject or challenge unauthenticated callers at the trust boundary.

threats.title: Missing or weak authorization enables privilege escalation
threats.description: Sample Web App Service does not enforce authorization checks per action, so an authenticated low-privilege actor may perform privileged operations.
threats.mitigation: Enforce server-side, deny-by-default authorization on every privileged action; apply least privilege and verify object-level access.

threats.title: Personal data is disclosed across a boundary
threats.description: Sample Web App Service carries personal data (credentials, pii) across a trust boundary, exposing it to parties that may not need it.
threats.mitigation: Share the minimum personal data necessary across the boundary; apply purpose limitation and a data-processing agreement for third parties.

threats.title: Untrusted input reaches the process without validation
threats.description: Sample Web App Service receives data from a less-trusted zone and may process it without validation, enabling injection or state corruption.
threats.mitigation: Validate and canonicalize all input at the boundary; use parameterized queries and context-aware output encoding.

threats.title: Internet-facing path can reach privileged/admin functionality
threats.description: Sample Web App Service is internet-facing and sits on a path toward trusted/admin functions; a flaw here can be leveraged to reach privileged operations.
threats.mitigation: Segment admin functionality behind separate authentication and network controls; never expose privileged operations on the public path.

threats.title: No rate limiting on an internet-facing process
threats.description: Sample Web App Service is internet-facing without rate limiting or quotas, so it can be overwhelmed by request floods.
threats.mitigation: Apply rate limiting, request quotas, timeouts and resource caps; place the service behind an edge/DoS-protection layer.

threats.title: Security-relevant actions are not auditable
threats.description: Sample Web App Service performs security-relevant actions but does not emit tamper-resistant audit logs, so actors can deny having acted.
threats.mitigation: Log security-relevant events with user identity, timestamp and outcome to an append-only, access-controlled store.

threats.title: Process may over-collect or over-expose personal data
threats.description: Sample Web App Service handles personal data; without purpose limitation it can collect or expose more than necessary.
threats.mitigation: Apply purpose limitation and least-privilege access to personal data; redact fields not required for the operation.

threats.title: Verbose errors or responses leak internal detail
threats.description: Sample Web App Service is internet-facing and may return verbose errors/stack traces that disclose internal structure to attackers.
threats.mitigation: Return generic error responses to clients; log detail server-side only; disable debug mode in production.

threats.title: Unauthenticated external actor can impersonate a legitimate user
threats.description: End User is an external entity whose requests are not strongly authenticated, so an attacker can impersonate it (e.g. credential stuffing, forged identity).
threats.mitigation: Require strong authentication for this actor (MFA where feasible), enforce password/credential policy, and rate-limit/lock out credential-stuffing attempts.

threats.title: Data subject may be unaware of processing (no consent signal)
threats.description: End User is a data subject whose awareness/consent for processing is not represented in the system.
threats.mitigation: Provide clear processing notices and capture a lawful basis/consent; expose data-subject rights (access, erasure).

threats.title: Sensitive data at rest is not encrypted
threats.description: SQLite Database stores sensitive data (credentials, pii) without encryption at rest, exposing it if the store is compromised.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt sensitive data at rest, manage keys separately from data, and restrict decrypt access to least privilege.

threats.title: Sensitive data is exposed in transit
threats.description: SQLite Database carries sensitive data (credentials, pii) across a boundary without encryption, so it can be intercepted.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt the channel end-to-end; minimize sensitive fields in transit and avoid placing them in URLs or logs.

threats.title: Personal data is disclosed across a boundary
threats.description: SQLite Database carries personal data (credentials, pii) across a trust boundary, exposing it to parties that may not need it.
threats.mitigation: Share the minimum personal data necessary across the boundary; apply purpose limitation and a data-processing agreement for third parties.

threats.title: Individuals are identifiable (no data minimisation/anonymisation)
threats.description: SQLite Database retains directly identifying personal data without minimisation or anonymisation, increasing re-identification risk.
threats.mitigation: Minimise collected fields, anonymise or aggregate where possible, and avoid storing direct identifiers you do not need.

threats.title: Data in transit can be tampered with across a trust boundary
threats.description: SQLite Database crosses a trust boundary without transport integrity (no TLS/encryption), so an on-path attacker can modify the data.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt and integrity-protect the channel (TLS 1.2+); reject plaintext transport for any boundary-crossing flow.

threats.title: Records are linkable across contexts (no pseudonymisation)
threats.description: SQLite Database stores personal data without pseudonymisation, so records about the same person can be linked across contexts.
threats.mitigation: Pseudonymise or tokenise identifiers at rest; separate linkable keys from personal data and restrict re-identification.

threats.title: No retention/governance controls on personal data (non-compliance)
threats.description: SQLite Database holds personal data without evidence of retention limits or access auditing, risking non-compliance with storage-limitation duties.
threats.mitigation: Define and enforce retention/deletion schedules, log access to personal data, and document the lawful basis and purpose.

threats.title: Stored data can be modified without detection
threats.description: SQLite Database persists data without integrity controls or change auditing, so unauthorized modification may go unnoticed.
threats.mitigation: Apply write authorization, integrity checks (hashing/signing) and tamper-evident audit logging to the store.

threats.title: Unbounded growth or connection exhaustion in the store
threats.description: SQLite Database can be driven to resource exhaustion (storage, connections) by unbounded writes from upstream processes.
threats.mitigation: Enforce connection pooling limits, quotas and input size caps upstream; monitor capacity and set alerts.

threats.title: Writes to the store are not attributable
threats.description: SQLite Database does not record who changed what, so repudiation of data changes is possible.
threats.mitigation: Record attributable, append-only change history for the store and protect it from the accounts that can write data.

threats.title: Personal data is disclosed across a boundary
threats.description: Third-party API carries personal data (payment, request) across a trust boundary, exposing it to parties that may not need it.
threats.mitigation: Share the minimum personal data necessary across the boundary; apply purpose limitation and a data-processing agreement for third parties.

threats.title: Data subject may be unaware of processing (no consent signal)
threats.description: Third-party API is a data subject whose awareness/consent for processing is not represented in the system.
threats.mitigation: Provide clear processing notices and capture a lawful basis/consent; expose data-subject rights (access, erasure).
